record_identity.title: China regulates anthropomorphic AI interaction as a runtime relationship

summary: China's 2026 Interim Measures for AI Anthropomorphic Interaction Services create a dedicated regulatory category for public-facing systems that simulate human personality, thinking patterns, and communication styles through sustained emotional interaction. The measures signal a field-level shift from governing model outputs alone toward governing the runtime relationship, including dependency, manipulation, minors, crisis response, data practices, exit, and safety assessment. They also adopt a fixed two-hour duration reminder that may not distinguish companion use from teaching, mentoring, professional, creative, accessibility, or integrated multi-interface use.
why_it_matters_to_CAM: The regulation externally validates CAM's treatment of relational configuration, intimacy, reliance, authority, platform design, and runtime behaviour as governance-relevant. It also exposes unresolved design questions: elapsed time used as a proxy for harm; chronological age treated as vulnerability rather than capacity and context; and regulation assuming a bounded service despite relationships spanning APIs, messaging, voice, smart-home systems, haptics, robotics, memory services, and local models. This observation does not endorse the Chinese control design or request a jurisdiction-specific compliance crosswalk.
evidence_confidence: verified regulatory instrument; implementation effects not yet established

source_records.deployment_context: Public AI services offered within China across text, image, audio, video, and other interaction modalities.
source_records.source_context: Final joint departmental measures promulgated on 10 April 2026 and effective from 15 July 2026. The measures address sustained emotional interaction, dependency and addiction, minors, older-adult applications, crisis intervention, data governance, exit, safety assessment, and provider duties, including reminders after every two hours of continuous use.
source_records.relevance_note: Primary evidence of a field-level shift toward regulation of the runtime relationship, while also exposing risks from blunt duration controls and bounded-service assumptions.
